**Key insight:** Most orders were paid in a single installment — **49,060 orders (58.3%)**, which is the peak for this period.

The pie chart below illustrates the distribution of orders by number of payment installments (1–5). It shows a clear concentration in single-installment payments, with progressively fewer orders choosing higher installment counts.

{chart_json}

---

| Payment Installments | Order Count | Share of Total |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 installment | **49,060** — the peak | **58.3%** |
| 2 installments | **12,389** | **14.7%** |
| 3 installments | **10,443** | **12.4%** |
| 4 installments | **7,088** | **8.4%** |
| 5 installments | **5,234** | **6.2%** |
| **Total** | **84,214** | **100%** |

Brief interpretation: Single-installment payments dominate (over half of orders). Two- and three-installment options together account for about 27% of orders, while four- and five-installment plans are comparatively rare. This suggests customers prefer paying upfront or in a small number of installments.
